title: Curve theta normalization and coherent diagonal Poincare line data
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], used only as a common ambient base. An input consists of a locally Noetherian actual base $T\to S$ [pqf-def-locnoeth], a smooth stable unpointed genus-$g$ curve $C\to T$, $g\ge2$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and an algebraic space $J$ over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] representing the total relative degree-zero Picard functor: on $R/S$ its value is the pairs $(a:R\to T,x\in\operatorname{Pic}_{C/T}(R,a))$ with degree identically zero [sk-def-picard-pic, def-pd-degree-morphism]. Properness and local finite presentation of $C/T$, consequences of stability, are retained for the degree interface. Its projection, identity, addition and inversion are the maps whose values on every scheme test are respectively the base map, trivial class, tensor product and dual class.

Use the existing small etale module model, actual fibre products, tensor pullbacks, axis trivializations, fibrewise algebraic triviality and universal rigidified Poincare representability [def-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-data]. The theta datum is an identity-preserving isomorphism $\lambda:J\simeq D$ over $T$, where $(D,P)$ represents the fibrewise algebraically trivial, identity-rigidified line functor of $J$. It is required to have the following theta normalization. On every etale $R\to T$ and for every degree-$(g-1)$ Picard class $N$ on $C_R$, let $\Theta_N$ be the scheme-theoretic image of the effective-divisor Abel map translated by $N^{-1}$. On every etale scheme chart $V$ of $J_R$, its ideal $H$ is characterized by $K\le H$ if and only if every scheme test $q:W\to V$ on which the Jacobian class times $N$ is the class of a finite flat degree-$(g-1)$ effective divisor annihilates $K$, meaning $K\le\ker(q)$. Divisors are the points of the relative Hilbert functor [def-pc-hilb-functor] with invertible ideal, and $\mathcal O(\Theta_N)=H^\vee$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle, def-sc-invertible-module]. There must be a line $L$ on $J_R$ restricting to these dual ideals on every etale scheme chart. Its normalized difference $m^*L\otimes p_1^*L^{-1}\otimes p_2^*L^{-1}\otimes\pi^*e^*L$ is axis-equivalent to $(1\times\lambda)^*P$ on $J_R\times_RJ_R$; the map to $J\times_TD$ is fixed by its two projections. This specifies the canonical theta principal polarization without choosing a global theta representative.

Define $d=(1,\lambda)$ by the actual fibre-product pairing and define $B=d^*P$ by the actual tensor pullback, with its specified identity trivialization induced by the two compatible Poincare axes. A scheme model is a $T$-scheme with an isomorphism to $J$ over $T$. Relative ampleness means that such a model exists and the ordinary corresponding line restricts to an invertible ample module over the inverse image of every affine open of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

A cartesian curve arrow consists of $T'\to T$ and a cartesian square $C'\to C$. Its canonical Jacobian map is characterized on every Picard class by the existing Picard pullback comparison. A coherent diagonal assignment gives the above theta and Poincare data for every input over $S$, these canonical Jacobian maps, and isomorphisms $a^*B\simeq B'$ preserving the specified identity trivializations. Its identity and composition equations use the actual tensor pullback identity and composition comparisons [def-sfb-space-derived-pullback]; thus they also impose the triple-fibre-product cocycle. These are definitions of data and predicates; no existence or line/ample property of $B$ is assumed.
